ferenceratops:study:1.title: A hidden diversity of ceratopsian dinosaurs in Late Cretaceous Europe (Nature, 2026)

facts.statement: Ferenceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) period.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: The type locality for Ferenceratops is the Sânpetru and Densuș-Ciula formations.
facts.quote: Type locality: Sânpetru and Densuș-Ciula formations

facts.statement: Ferenceratops fossils were found in Romania.
facts.quote: Country: Romania

facts.statement: Ferenceratops is classified as a ceratopsian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Notes: A ceratopsian.

facts.statement: The genus Ferenceratops was established by Maidment et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: authority: Maidment et al., 2026

facts.statement: Fossils originally attributed to Ferenceratops were previously referred to the ornithopod Zalmoxes.
facts.quote: These fossils, in addition to many other isolated or associated remains, were originally referred to the rhabdodontid ornithopod Zalmoxes.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses suggest Ferenceratops is a close relative of Ajkaceratops and part of a distinct lineage of European ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses based on new remains of Ajkaceratops suggest Ferenceratops was a close relative of this genus, as part of a distinct lineage of previously unrecognized European ceratopsians.

facts.statement: The genus Zalmoxes, which included the species later moved to Ferenceratops, was described in 2003 by Weishampel and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2003, David B. Weishampel and colleagues described the new genus Zalmoxes based on fossil material found in many Maastrichtian-aged localities throughout the Hațeg Basin of Transylvania, Romania.

facts.statement: The specific name shqiperorum honors the people of Shqiperia, the Albanian name for their nation.
facts.quote: The specific name honors the people of Shqiperia, which is the name used by Albanians for their nation.

facts.statement: The holotype of Zalmoxes shqiperorum (now Ferenceratops) is a partial skeleton housed at the Natural History Museum in London.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of this species, housed at the Natural History Museum in London, England as NHMUK PV R 4900, is a partial skeleton, including an incomplete right dentary and dorsal (trunk) vertebra, left scapula and coracoid, part of an ilium, a complete right and distal (bottom end) left ischium, and a complete left femur.

facts.statement: The material comprising the holotype was originally described in 1928 by Baron Franz Nopcsa.
facts.quote: It had been described in 1928 by Baron Franz Nopcsa as "individual I" in a publication discussing Rhabdodon.

facts.statement: A new partial skull referable to Ajkaceratops was described in 2026, which helped clarify the identity of Ferenceratops.
facts.quote: In 2026, Susannah Maidment and colleagues described a new partial skull from the Csehbánya Formation of Hungary referable to Ajkaceratops kozmai, a putative ceratopsian dinosaur whose identity as a member of this clade had been debated in the years prior.

facts.statement: Maidment et al. transferred Zalmoxes shqiperorum to the new genus Ferenceratops because the placement of Z. robustus was unstable.
facts.quote: Since the phylogenetic placement of Z. robustus was less stable than Z. shqiperorum, and in some analyses remained an iguanodont close to Rhabodon, Maidment et al. opted to give the new generic name Ferenceratops to "Z." shqiperorum.

facts.statement: The genus name Ferenceratops is derived from the birth name of Baron Franz Nopcsa.
facts.quote: This name is derived from Ferenc, which is the birth name of Baron Franz Nopcsa, a notable Hungarian palaeontologist whose work included the study of Haţeg Basin dinosaurs, including the holotype of this species.

facts.statement: In 2026, Maidment et al. recognized only one referred specimen, a pelvis (UBB SPZ-2), as belonging to Ferenceratops.
facts.quote: Maidment et al. (2026) only recognized UBB SPZ-2, a referred pelvis, as a suitable referred specimen of Ferenceratops, given the identical anatomy of the ischia.

facts.statement: Most previously referred material was not considered referable to Ferenceratops due to lack of overlap with the holotype.
facts.quote: As much of the remaining referred material does not overlap with the holotype and needs more thorough study, it was not considered referable to this genus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether material previously assigned to rhabdodontids like Zalmoxes actually belongs to multiple distinct taxa, including both iguanodonts and ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Since many rhabdodontid species are known from material collected bone beds, there is often a possibility that the material actually belongs to multiple distinct taxa, with some deriving from iguanodonts and others from ceratopsians.

facts.statement: Ferenceratops is diagnosed by a unique combination of anatomical characters distinguishing it from other taxa.
facts.quote: In their 2026 reassessment of Ferenceratops, Maidment and colleagues diagnosed F. shqiperorum with a unique combination of anatomical characters that distinguished it from other taxa.

facts.statement: Ferenceratops has a narrow scapula with a strap-like blade and a prominent, upwardly concave acromial process.
facts.quote: These include a scapula that is narrow, with a strap-like blade, expansion at the end, and a prominent, upwardly concave acromial process (articulation point for the clavicle.

facts.statement: The ischium of Ferenceratops is gently curved and lacks an obturator process.
facts.quote: Finally, the ischium is gently curved and does not have an obturator process.

facts.statement: No ornithopod synapomorphies were identified in the Ferenceratops holotype, and several features are consistent with ceratopsians.
facts.quote: The authors emphasized that no ornithopod synapomorphies could be identified in the F. shqiperorum holotype, and several features are much more consistent with ceratopsians.

facts.statement: Researchers placed Ferenceratops within the Ceratopsia based on a phylogenetic analysis by Maidment et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: Maidment et al. (2026) used the phylogenetic dataset of Han et al. (2017), which was used to test the relationships of the early ceratopsian Yinlong.

facts.statement: The genus Ferenceratops belongs to the parent group Ceratopsia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ceratopsia

facts.statement: Ferenceratops is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Ferenceratops lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Ferenceratops have been found in the Sânpetru and Densuș-Ciula formations in Romania.
facts.quote: Ferenceratops is known from remains found in the Sânpetru and Densuș-Ciula formations of Romania

facts.statement: The environment where Ferenceratops lived was subtropical with fluctuating rainy and dry seasons.
facts.quote: The climate of this paleoenvironment has been interpreted as subtropical, with palaeosols (ancient soil layers), flora types, and stable isotopes indicating fluctuating rainy and dry seasons.

facts.statement: Carbon isotope evidence suggests Ferenceratops lived in a dry woodland environment.
facts.quote: Carbon isotopes imply the conditions were consistent with a dry woodland.

facts.statement: Oxygen isotope data suggests a mean annual temperature of 20 to 25 °C for the habitat of Ferenceratops.
facts.quote: A mean annual temperature between 20 and 25 °C is suggested by oxygen isotopes.

facts.statement: Ferenceratops shared its habitat with titanosaurian sauropods and feathered theropods like Balaur and Elopteryx.
facts.quote: Both formations are characterized by titanosaurian sauropods (such as Magyarosaurus, Paludititan, Petrustitan, and Uriash) and feathered theropods (dromaeosaurids, troodontids, Balaur, and Elopteryx).

facts.statement: The Sânpetru Formation also contained the ankylosaur Struthiosaurus and the hadrosauromorph Telmatosaurus.
facts.quote: Other dinosaurs from the Sânpetru Formation include the ankylosaur Struthiosaurus and the hadrosauromorph Telmatosaurus.

facts.statement: The fauna included the giant pterosaur Hatzegopteryx, various crocodilians, snakes, lizards, turtles, birds, mammals, amphibians, and fish.
facts.quote: Other animals of the fauna include the giant azhdarchid pterosaur Hatzegopteryx, various mesoeucrocodylians (Allodaposuchus, Acynodon, Doratodon, and Musturzabalsuchus), various snakes, lizards, and turtles, birds, multituberculate mammals, albanerpetontid and anuran (frogs) amphibians, and several fish.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ferenceratops belongs to the Rhabdodontidae or Ceratopsia, as it was traditionally classified as an ornithopod.
facts.quote: The holotype of Ferenceratops (previously "Zalmoxes") shqiperorum has traditionally been regarded as belonging to an ornithopod, specifically a member of the Rhabdodontidae.
